About the Role

Neural Concept accelerates the full engineering simulation cycle. Our AI platform compresses the time from design change to validated result, so engineering teams can explore more, iterate faster, and ship better products. The Vertical Solutions team turns that capability into production-grade, domain-specific solutions for our customers.

As a Senior CAE and AI Expert, you will own the simulation workflows, benchmarks, and solution assets that sit at the heart of what we deliver. Your work will land directly inside the engineering processes of leading automotive OEMs and consumer electronics companies — accelerating the entire cycle from geometry change through to crash, safety, and drop test results.

What You Will Do

  • Own vertical solution assets end-to-end. Design and develop simulation workflows, validation benchmarks, and solution templates for automotive structural analysis (crash, occupant safety, pedestrian safety) and consumer electronics durability (drop test, vibration). Take assets from concept through to handover to Sales and Customer Success.

  • Accelerate the full simulation pipeline. Map the complete cycle — design change, automated meshing, solver configuration, job execution, and design optimisation — onto Neural Concept's platform. Define accuracy and speed requirements, validate against benchmark data, and deliver repeatable, production-grade workflows using tools such as ABAQUS, LS-Dyna, Radioss, Hypermesh, ANSA, and Simlab.

  • Write Python automation and tooling. Script data preprocessing, solution packaging, and workflow integration. Maintain solution reproducibility standards and contribute to internal tooling libraries.

  • Drive the product roadmap from the field. Partner with Product and Engineering to surface simulation-specific platform requirements, validate new capabilities, and feed real-world use cases directly into development priorities.

Who You Are

  • 5–8 years of hands-on FEA simulation experience, in the application of vehicle crash, drop test, pedestrian and/or passenger safety, delivering production-quality models in automotive or consumer electronics environments

  • Deep expertise in leading Mechanical pre-solve-post tools, such as: ABAQUS, LS-Dyna, Radioss, Hypermesh, Simlab, ANSA, Meta, d3plot

  • Strong command of structural non-linear simulation: implicit/explicit solvers, contact formulations, material models, failure criteria

  • Demonstrated experience in automotive safety simulations (crash, occupant safety, pedestrian safety) or product durability testing (drop test, shock, vibration)

  • Experience with end-to-end simulation workflows: CAD preparation → Meshing → Solving → Post-processing → Visualization

  • Scripting and programming: Python (preferred); C++, Java, or C# also valued. Exposure to open-source tools (e.g., OpenFOAM, FEniCSx) and pre/post tools (e.g., Gmsh, ParaView) a plus.

  • Able to own deliverables independently and communicate complex technical concepts clearly to non-specialist audiences

  • Proficiency in both written and spoken English, with the ability to articulate technical complexity with clarity.

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with AI-assisted simulation acceleration, design optimisation, or parametric study automation

  • Comfort with Git and modern dev environments/IDEs; basic CI for validation of templates and scripts

  • Master HPC and Cloud resources. Execute and refine complex simulations within high-performance computing environments, effectively deploying GPU acceleration to maximize workflow performance.

What You Get

  • Competitive salary and benefits

  • Training budget — we believe continuous education is essential for you and for us.

  • Work directly with a world-class engineering team that sets high standards and means it.

  • Visible, high-impact work inside a collaborative, multicultural environment where your contributions are recognised.

  • Real influence on how the world’s best engineering organisations use AI to design better products — faster and more sustainably.

  • Ample GPU/CPU resources via HPC and Cloud for your simulation and AI workloads.

  • Hybrid working model — 3 days in the Lausanne office, flexible hours, and we care about output not schedules.

We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and we're committed to building a diverse and inclusive environment where you can thrive.

data.description:
About machineMD

At machineMD in Bern we’re on a mission to radically improve the measurement of brain function through standardized, automated, quantitative exams. Our signature product, neos™, is the world’s first non-invasive neuro-ophthalmoscope for fast, automated assessment of eye movements and pupils. Founded at the University Hospital of Bern, Switzerland, we’ve grown into a startup of 25 engineers, clinicians, scientists, and specialists working side by side. We aim to bring the diagnostic quality of highly trained specialists into secondary and primary care settings everywhere.

We’re building neurodiagnostics for the next generation with our neos™ device and oculometrics software. As our Software Test Engineer, you’ll have room to make a visible difference in how we test. Find a gap, develop an approach, and put it to work, whether that means automating a manual check, building better test data, or connecting tests across the system. You’ll develop our test automation with support from developers, requirements engineers, and testers. Our existing test infrastructure gives you a starting point, with room to introduce your own ideas and additional tools as you connect and improve how we test.

The Role

You’ll help us understand how neos™ behaves when its components work together—and where they fail. Your main contribution will be developing automated tests, test data, and scripts that make complex scenarios repeatable and problems easier to diagnose. You’ll work alongside developers and use the domain expertise and manual testing provided by requirements engineers and testers.

  • Pragmatic Improvements – assess our current testing setup with the team, identify the biggest weaknesses, and tackle them step by step. Build on what works, try useful approaches, and let a broader test concept grow from the improvements you put into practice.

  • Automation Across the System – develop automated tests for complex, distributed systems across different frameworks and technologies, covering multiple components, interfaces, and end-to-end scenarios beyond UI testing.

  • Test Infrastructure – build on and improve our physical and software-based test environments. Introduce tools and setups where they make testing more effective, and keep them documented so tests remain repeatable and usable by others.

  • Coordination & Code Quality – work hands-on with developers to implement automation, coordinate contributions, and review the quality of test code. Connect individual improvements so our testing becomes more consistent and easier to extend over time.

  • Verification & Validation – contribute to V&V plans, protocols, reports, and evidence, and coordinate activities with the relevant specialists. Help keep testing, requirements, and documentation aligned in a medical device environment.

What We Look For

Experience

  • Solid practical experience in software engineering, including designing, implementing, debugging, and maintaining software. You can understand existing codebases and develop clear, well-structured solutions that others can maintain and extend.

  • Experience with some of our core technologies (Python, C#/.NET, C++ and Flutter/Dart) is a plus. Python and pytest are particularly useful for test automation, and you’re willing to learn the technologies needed for the task.

  • Practical experience developing automated tests across different system levels, with the programming skills to implement, understand, and review test code.

  • Experience with verification and validation of medical devices or familiarity with ISO 13485 is a plus.

Qualifications

  • Solid software testing fundamentals at ISTQB Foundation Level or equivalent knowledge, including test planning, test design, and requirements coverage.

  • Vocational training or a higher degree in computer science, software engineering, medical informatics, or a related technical field.

  • Fluent English (minimum strong B2, ideally C1); German or French language skills are a plus for on-site collaboration.

Eligibility to work in Switzerland (Swiss/EU/EFTA work permit).

How You Work

  • Systems Thinker – you want to understand how neos™ works as a whole, from its software and hardware to the tests and data behind it. you choose practical improvements as our product and testing continue to develop.

  • Curiosity & a Detective’s Instinct – you notice when something doesn’t quite add up and enjoy following the clues. You question assumptions, explore unusual scenarios, and keep digging until you can explain and reproduce what you’ve found.

  • Close the Gaps – you enjoy getting your hands dirty and following a problem across disciplines. When progress depends on something outside your usual remit, you’re willing to learn, lend a hand.

  • Collaborative Spirit – you work closely with colleagues, share what you know and what you’re unsure about, and address difficult topics openly. You listen with curiosity, give and receive candid feedback, and make room for different perspectives.

  • Shaper Mentality & Growth Mindset – you want to shape how testing works, take responsibility, and build missing skills quickly. You’re curious about neurodiagnostics and ready to learn from experts and real-world use cases.

Working at machineMD

  • Based in Bern, Switzerland, with roughly 80% of your working time on-site (approximately four days a week at full-time employment) and Monday as our shared anchor day.

  • Collaborative, in-person working, with flexibility to do your best work.

Our Four Pillars of Integrity guide how we work together:

  • Radical Responsibility: Own our choices.

  • Feeling Our Feelings: Name and honour our emotions.

  • Candor: Speak and listen with honesty.

  • Clear Agreements: Make and keep clear commitments.

Life’s too short to work on boring stuff. If you want to connect ideas, people, and technology to advance brain diagnostics in a dynamic startup, let’s talk!

How to Apply

Send your CV and a short note about a project or task from your career that you enjoyed a lot, and explain why.

We welcome applications from all qualified individuals regardless of gender, age, background, or orientation. Direct applications only, no recruiters please.

We’re excited to meet you!

Who We Are

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

Evaluation is the core of everything we do. We build from the evals: we define how success will be measured before developing a capability, and use the results to guide training, model selection and deployment. We already have hundreds of evaluations spanning domain knowledge, commerce and gaming, with plans to expand their coverage, depth and scale.

This work builds on ProLLM, the public benchmarking platform we ran for real-world use cases until our coding assistant benchmarks became saturated. Since then it has been a private benchmarking platform for Prosus companies. We plan to open it again to publish our commerce benchmarks, covering both agentic and decision-making tasks.

We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own the development of these evaluations and the platform that runs them. The work involves defining meaningful tasks, curating evaluation data, implementing reliable scoring, investigating model behaviour and making results useful for research and product decisions.

In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work directly with applied scientists, training engineers and domain experts. You’ll help teams contribute evaluations and build the infrastructure and automation needed to run them throughout model development.

In the first three months, we expect you to take technical ownership of part of the evaluation platform, deliver a set of new or improved evaluations with curated data and calibrated difficulty, and work with scientists to use them in a training or release decision.

What the role involves

  • Design evaluations with scientists and domain experts, translating intended capabilities into representative tasks, datasets and success criteria. Cover current applications and capabilities we want future models to acquire.

  • Curate evaluation data and calibrate task difficulty, so that evaluations are neither saturated nor out of reach and still separate models of different quality. Work with domain experts on sourcing, annotation and review, within data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy requirements.

  • Own the development and operation of the evaluation platform across training checkpoints, deployed models and external baselines. Support distributed execution, reproducible configurations, trace inspection and comparison of results, while managing runtime and cost.

  • Develop programmatic checks, outcome-based scoring and LLM-based graders. Calibrate automated judgments against expert reviews, investigate disagreements and test whether graders reward superficial answers or reject valid solutions.

  • Analyse model outputs and agent trajectories, including tool calls, environment state and task outcomes. Distinguish model failures from problems in the evaluation, quantify uncertainty and explain what changed between versions.

  • Maintain versioned tasks, datasets, graders and environments, with protected held-out tests and contamination checks. Expand coverage as models improve, retaining useful regression tests and adding harder tasks where existing tests no longer distinguish performance.

  • Prepare commerce benchmarks for public release on ProLLM, including public mirror sets and evaluation code, where the data can be shared.

  • Integrate evaluations into training and release workflows, with dashboards and regression checks that support concrete decisions. Work with portfolio teams to establish whether offline improvements correspond to better outcomes in online experiments.

  • Build tools and agents that help generate candidate tasks, run evaluations and investigate failures, validating their outputs before adoption. Review contributions and mentor engineers so teams can extend the suite consistently.

Minimum qualifications

  • At least five years of ML or software engineering experience, including substantial hands-on work building and evaluating ML systems.

  • Experience owning evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or model-quality systems that informed training or deployment decisions.

  • Strong Python and experience with PyTorch, Transformers or comparable ML libraries, alongside reliable production software development.

  • Practical knowledge of experimental design and statistics, including sampling, uncertainty, repeated trials and comparisons across model versions.

  • Experience running inference or evaluation workloads at scale and debugging failures across models, data, scoring code and infrastructure.

  • Clear communication and the ability to turn ambiguous results into defensible recommendations.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with language-model training or post-training.

  • Experience with agent or gaming environments.

  • Experience with human evaluation, LLM-as-judge calibration, recommendation metrics or online experimentation.

  • Contributions to evaluation frameworks, public benchmarks or research.

What we offer

  • Ownership of the evaluation platform and the evaluations that guide LCM’s research, training and deployment.

  • Access to proprietary domain data, GPU infrastructure and external models for comparison.

  • Direct collaboration with researchers, engineers and portfolio teams, with scope to publish methods and benchmarks, including through ProLLM, where the work can be shared.

  • Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

  • Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

  • A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

  • Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

If you want to build the evaluations that shape what a foundation model learns, we’d like to hear from you. Please include examples of evaluations or platforms you have built, how you established that their results were reliable, and the decisions those results informed.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

We’re looking for experienced applied scientists in two tracks: pre-training, and post-training and continual learning. Each scientist will own a focused research direction within a track. The areas below describe the team’s research agenda; we are looking for depth in one or more of them.

The role involves designing experiments, writing the code to run them, analysing results and developing training methods that other teams can use. Scientists own the research questions, training objectives and evidence needed to decide whether a change works, and work with ML engineers to turn successful experiments into reliable training runs. We are a team of around 30 engineers with a flat structure, working directly with portfolio companies to define problems, evaluate models and bring successful work into production.

In the first three months, the expectation is to establish strong baselines in a chosen research area, develop and evaluate an improvement, and work with the relevant teams to test it in a downstream application.

Track 1: Pre-training

This track focuses on continued pre-training of open-weight models on commerce data, including how we represent that data, allocate training compute and transfer capabilities to smaller models. Research areas include:

  • Studying scaling behaviour, data mixtures and compute allocation to decide what goes into the next training run.

  • Developing mid-training methods, including data refinement, annealing schedules, context extension and alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants.

  • Designing training sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, and studying how representations transfer across companies, languages and commerce categories.

  • Building synthetic data pipelines and measuring their contribution through controlled comparisons with real data.

  • Distilling the base model into smaller models, including through on-policy distillation, and measuring the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency.

  • Developing evaluations that help select pre-training runs and predict downstream performance, including checks for temporal leakage, generalisation to new users and items, and retention of existing capabilities.

  • Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation: pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data, using synthetic and real tables and comparing results with established tabular methods.

Relevant experience includes continued pre-training or mid-training, data mixture research, scaling laws, tokenisation, entity representations, distillation, or tabular foundation models such as TabPFN and TabICL.

Track 2: Post-training and continual learning

This track focuses on adapting LCM to commerce tasks and learning from interactions after deployment. The goal is to turn signals from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio into regular updates to model weights, while retaining the capabilities the model has already learned. Research areas include:

  • Developing post-training methods using supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation such as DPO, and reinforcement learning with verifiable or learned rewards, including GRPO and PPO.

  • Learning from session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback. This includes data selection, credit assignment and reward design that account for exposure bias, delayed outcomes and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value.

  • Studying how to combine new interactions with historical data, how frequently to update models, when an update is ready for deployment, and how to preserve performance as user behaviour and catalogues change.

  • Building RL environments with simulated users, catalogues and multi-step commerce tasks, including inspecting trajectories, validating rewards and testing whether improvements in simulation transfer to real interactions.

  • Developing reward models and LLM-based graders, calibrating them against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and testing for reward hacking, sycophancy and excessive concentration on popular items.

  • Training decision models for rankings, offers and promotions using contextual bandits or offline RL, with off-policy evaluation to estimate value and uncertainty, identify gaps in the available evidence and inform controlled online experiments.

  • Developing automated experiments that propose and test changes to training methods, prompts, tools or agent control flow, evaluated on held-out tasks and regression tests before acceptance.

Relevant experience includes language-model post-training, reinforcement learning, reward modelling, agent training environments, continual learning, or offline RL and bandits applied to real decisions. The training experience required will depend on the research direction.

Responsibilities across both tracks

  • Define success with portfolio teams and evaluate models against strong baselines, including existing production systems, accounting for inference cost, latency and the business outcome the model is meant to improve.

  • Design reproducible experiments with appropriate ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis, using future-period and held-out evaluations, and test whether offline improvements hold online.

  • Work with data and engineering teams on provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories.

  • Publish research and contribute models, benchmarks, environments and training methods to open source where the work and data can be shared.

  • Mentor colleagues, review experiment designs and communicate findings clearly enough to support training and deployment decisions.

Minimum qualifications

  • A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field.

  • At least five years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with hands-on experience designing and running model-training experiments. For Track 1, this should include pre-training or mid-training of language models. For Track 2, it should include language-model post-training, or reinforcement learning and decision-model training relevant to the specialisation.

  • Evidence of original research through papers, released models, public benchmarks, open-source projects or significant research contributions to deployed systems.

  • Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with experience implementing experiments and debugging training runs in a shared research codebase. Work on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training.

  • Sound experimental judgment, including strong baselines, statistical analysis and the willingness to report negative results.

  • Clear written and verbal communication.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience implementing and debugging training methods in frameworks such as Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, NeMo RL, verl or OpenRLHF, depending on the chosen track.

  • Research in recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs or user behaviour modelling.

  • Experience with synthetic data, model distillation or compression for production.

  • Experience working with marketplace or commerce data and evaluating changes through online experiments.

What we offer

  • Autonomy to design experiments and make technical decisions within your research direction.

  • Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking.

  • The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people.

  • Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

  • Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

  • Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

How to apply

  • Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation, including pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data.

Post-training and continual learning

We train LCM for commerce tasks and a range of agent applications, including customer-facing assistants and agents that carry out business operations. We also develop continual learning methods that turn new interactions into regular updates to model weights. Work may include:

  • Developing supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation and reinforcement learning methods, using verifiable outcomes or learned reward models.

  • Turning session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback into training examples and rewards, accounting for exposure bias, delayed feedback and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value.

  • Studying data selection, replay and update frequency so models learn from new interactions without losing established capabilities.

  • Training and evaluating decision models that choose rankings, offers and promotions, using offline learning and off-policy evaluation to estimate policy value and uncertainty and inform controlled online experiments.

  • Training models for multi-turn conversations and multi-step agent workflows, including understanding user intent, planning, tool use, maintaining context, recovering from errors and verifying outcomes. This includes building RL environments with simulated users and catalogues, and testing whether gains transfer to real interactions within defined permissions and business rules.

  • Calibrating reward models and LLM-based graders against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and investigating reward hacking and other unintended effects.

  • Developing automated experimentation methods that propose and test changes to training recipes, prompts, tools or agent control flow, with held-out evaluations and regression checks.

How we evaluate the work

Research should produce evidence that supports a training or deployment decision. We use strong baselines, including existing production systems, and weigh model quality against compute requirements, inference cost and latency.

Experiments should be reproducible, with ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis. They must account for temporal leakage, changes in the data distribution and differences between companies and markets. Negative results are valuable when they explain a limitation or stop further investment in an approach that does not work.

The work also involves data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories, together with our data and engineering teams.

In the first three months, we expect you to establish a focused research programme, resolve an important training or evaluation question, and work with the relevant teams to test the resulting method in a downstream application.

Minimum qualifications

  • A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field.

  • At least eight years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with at least four years leading research directions that were published or reached production.

  • Substantial experience developing and training models, with deep expertise in pre-training, post-training or reinforcement learning relevant to the areas above.

  • A record of original contributions, shown through research papers, released models, benchmarks, open-source projects or significant advances in deployed systems.

  • Scientific leadership: choosing research directions, resolving difficult technical questions and helping experienced colleagues make better decisions.

  • Sound experimental and statistical judgment, including examples where the evidence changed your approach and the ability to recognise when the evidence does not support a conclusion.

  • Strong Python and PyTorch skills and the ability to work independently in a shared research codebase. Research on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training.

  • Clear communication and a collaborative approach to disagreement, review and mentoring.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs, continual learning, synthetic data, distillation or tabular foundation models.

  • Familiarity with commerce data and online experimentation.

  • We do not expect expertise in every area.

What we offer

  • Influence over LCM’s research agenda and which questions the team invests in.

  • Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking.

  • The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people.

  • Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

  • An uncapped budget to recruit and mentor research interns for your projects, with access to candidates through our connections with leading universities.

  • Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

  • A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

  • Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

How to apply

Please include examples of research or deployed work that show your contribution, the decisions involved and the evidence used to evaluate the results, and indicate which research area best matches your depth.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, ecommerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

We’re looking for a senior data engineer to build and operate LCM’s training-data platform, covering acquisition, processing, synthetic generation, quality evaluation and dataset versioning.

Our core data includes events, sessions, orders, catalogues and feedback, supplemented by external sources and generated examples. In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work with scientists and ML engineers to turn these sources into reproducible datasets and measure how changes to the data affect model performance. You’ll also build tools and agents that automate preparation, task design and quality analysis.

In the first three months, we expect you to take ownership of a part of the platform, such as a pipeline, the dataset versioning layer or the quality checks, deliver a reproducible dataset that a research project uses in a training run, and work with scientists to measure how your data changes affect model quality.

What the role involves

  • Build acquisition and processing pipelines for portfolio data and relevant public and licensed sources, including connectors and content extraction. Turn commerce records into ordered histories and link behaviour to outcomes without leaking future information.

  • Develop the shared platform for inspecting sources, configuring processing and publishing training datasets. Operate distributed workflows, monitor reliability and cost, and implement access controls and retention requirements.

  • Work with scientists, engineers and the relevant teams on data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories.

  • Implement dataset versioning and lineage across source snapshots, processing code and dataset configurations, so releases can be reproduced and traced to the training runs that used them.

  • Build quality checks for completeness, freshness, duplication, extraction accuracy and coverage. Combine automated checks with sampled review to investigate problems that aggregate metrics can miss.

  • Provide tools for source tagging, sampling and weighting, and maintain evaluation datasets with temporal splits and overlap checks. Work with scientists on controlled comparisons to establish whether data changes improve model quality.

  • Build synthetic data pipelines supporting pre- and post-training, including instruction examples, preference data and agent trajectories. Implement generation, validation, scoring and filtering. Work with the research team to measure how the generated data affects model performance, and manage generation throughput and cost.

  • Build agents that turn catalogue sources into training datasets: propose tasks based on available data and target model capabilities, configure processing and generation, curate outputs and investigate quality failures. Keep agent actions traceable and validate proposed changes before dataset release.

Minimum qualifications

  • At least five years of relevant data engineering experience, including ownership of substantial production pipelines.

  • Strong Python and SQL, with experience writing tested, maintainable code.

  • Hands-on experience with distributed processing using Spark, Ray, Beam or a comparable framework.

  • Experience with cloud storage, workflow orchestration and operating pipelines through source changes, failures and backfills.

  • Practical knowledge of data quality, versioning and lineage, and the ability to translate evolving research requirements into reliable implementations.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with LLM datasets, commerce data, content extraction, synthetic data generation or agents for data tasks.

  • Experience with AWS, Databricks or EMR.

  • Strong distributed-data engineering experience is welcome without prior experience on an LLM team.

What we offer

  • Ownership of the platform supplying LCM’s training and evaluation data, with direct collaboration with researchers and ML engineers.

  • Access to proprietary commerce datasets, distributed processing infrastructure and models for generation and evaluation.

  • Scope to make technical decisions and build reusable tools across portfolio companies.

  • Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

  • Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

  • A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

  • Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

If you’ve built data systems at scale and want to help shape what a foundation model can do, we’d like to hear from you. Tell us about something you’ve built, the challenges involved and the difference it made.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. And we’re only just getting started!

Our Team

We are an enthusiastic, passionate and hardworking team of ≈ 100 people. Our founding team has strong entrepreneurial experience building and scaling web products from 0 to IPO.

Alexis Soulopoulos [CEO]

• Co-founder/CFO @SoftOne (exited)

Your Role

Most LLM roles stop at experimentation.

Here, the models you improve power experiences for 50M+ users.

Most of our traffic runs on self-hosted, fine-tuned open-weight models. On our internal roleplay evals, our smaller fine-tuned models can outperform much larger off-the-shelf models. Your job is to make them better.

You’ll join a small AI team led by Marco, our LLM Tech Lead, working closely with our CTO, Product, Web and DevOps teams. You’ll work across data, post-training, evals, and model behavior, taking ideas from failure analysis to production.

The problems are real: personalization, character consistency, long conversations, better evals, multilingual behavior, and faster training cycles.

If you want to shape model behavior at consumer scale, this is the role.

Key Responsibilities

  • Fine-tune open-weight LLMs using SFT, LoRA/QLoRA and post-training methods such as DPO and GRPO

  • Diagnose model failures and turn them into experiments. Decide whether the answer is better data, post-training, prompting or classifiers

  • Build training data and evals that directly shape what gets trained next

  • You can take work beyond notebooks into production

  • You use AI tools daily in your own engineering work

  • You are fully comfortable working with uncensored models and explicit NSFW content, including harmful material when developing and evaluating moderation system

Bonus points

  • Experience with conversational AI, roleplay products, or highly personalized consumer AI

  • Multilingual LLMs

  • Moderation, safety, or adversarial testing

  • Multimodal models

  • Open-source LLM / post-training contributions

🌍 Global Impact: Top-tier user growth, real-world adoption, and cultural relevance

Wil jij ervaren hoe het is om AI niet alleen technisch te begrijpen, maar ook écht werkend te maken binnen een organisatie? Heb jij interesse in AI, data, technologie én consultancy? Dan is deze stage binnen ons Data & AI-team misschien wel jouw volgende stap!

Vanaf februari 2027 zoeken wij een stagiair(e) Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Data Science die gedurende 3 tot 12 maanden meewerkt aan interne AI-initiatieven binnen IG&H. Met deze stage krijg je de kans om jouw technische vaardigheden te combineren met consultancyvaardigheden: van het bouwen of onderzoeken van AI-oplossingen tot het ophalen van behoeften bij stakeholders en het ondersteunen van AI-adoptie binnen onze organisatie.

Wat ga je doen?

Tijdens deze leerzame stage ga je aan de slag met interne AI-oplossingen en innovatieprojecten. Afhankelijk van de behoefte vanuit de business werk je zelfstandig aan projecten binnen het team. Je kunt bijvoorbeeld bijdragen aan:

  • het ontwikkelen of verbeteren van AI-tools die interne processen efficiënter maken;

  • het in kaart brengen van processen binnen interne teams en onderzoeken waar AI kan helpen/ondersteunen;

  • het ondersteunen van AI-adoptie binnen IG&H, bijvoorbeeld door mee te denken over trainingen, communicatie of praktische toepassingen van tools zoals Copilot;

  • het doen van onderzoek naar nieuwe AI-producten, toepassingen of proposities;

  • het vertalen van technische mogelijkheden naar concrete businesswaarde;

  • samenwerken met andere collega’s binnen Data & AI.

Over het team

Wij helpen onze klanten innoveren en gebruikmaken van de nieuwste data- en AI-technologie. Ons Data & AI-team bestaat uit ruim 40 data-experts, waaronder Data Scientists, Data Engineers en Consultants. Samen realiseren zij innovatieve data-, analytics- en AI-oplossingen voor klanten in Retail, Financial Services en Health. Het team groeit snel en heeft de ambitie om verder uit te bouwen tot een van de meest toonaangevende Data & AI-praktijken van Nederland. Die groei komt voort uit ons succes: klanten kiezen steeds vaker voor IG&H vanwege onze combinatie van strategisch inzicht, technische expertise en pragmatische executie. We werken aan projecten die direct bijdragen aan betere besluitvorming, efficiëntere processen en nieuwe businessmodellen. Voor professionals die impact willen maken is dit een omgeving waar ondernemerschap, innovatie en persoonlijke ontwikkeling centraal staan. Hier bouw je niet alleen mee aan de toekomst van onze klanten, maar ook aan de verdere groei van het Data & AI-team zelf.

Wat wij verwachten van jou:

We zoeken een leergierig en analytisch sterk persoon die energie krijgt van AI, data science en consultancy. Je vindt het leuk om technologie te begrijpen, maar minstens zo belangrijk: je wilt ontdekken hoe je technologie toepasbaar maakt voor mensen en organisaties. Je brengt mee:

  • Je volgt bij voorkeur een masteropleiding in de richting van Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Computer Science, Econometrie, Natuurkunde, Wiskunde, Engineering of een vergelijkbare technische/kwantitatieve studie;

  • Je hebt ervaring met Python;

  • Je vindt het leuk om met stakeholders in gesprek te gaan en behoeften goed uit te vragen;

  • Je kunt technische onderwerpen helder uitleggen aan mensen met verschillende achtergronden;

  • Je bent sociaal, nieuwsgierig en proactief;

  • Je spreekt en schrijft goed Nederlands en Engels;

  • Je bent vanaf februari 2027 beschikbaar voor 32 tot 40 uur per week.

Ervaring met SQL, API’s, Azure of AI-tools zoals Copilot is mooi meegenomen, maar geen harde eis. Belangrijker vinden we dat je nieuwsgierig bent, snel leert en zin hebt om jezelf inhoudelijk te ontwikkelen.

Wat wij jou bieden:

Bij IG&H krijg je de kans om in korte tijd veel te leren binnen een ambitieus en betrokken Data & AI-team. Je werkt aan een eigen project, krijgt goede begeleiding en maakt kennis met de praktijk van consultancy en technologie. Verder bieden wij jou:

  • Een stage binnen een Great Place to Work met een prettige sfeer en enthousiaste collega’s;

  • De kans om mee te werken aan concrete AI-initiatieven binnen IG&H;

  • Je werkt samen met ervaren collega’s binnen het Data & AI-team;

  • Begeleiding door een buddy en mentor vanuit de organisatie;

  • Veel ruimte om jouw technische én consultancyvaardigheden te ontwikkelen;

  • Een inspirerend kantoor in Utrecht;

  • De mogelijkheid om na enige tijd in overleg deels thuis te werken;

  • Teamactiviteiten, borrels en een open, ondernemende werksfeer;

  • Een contract van 3 tot 12 maanden en een vergoeding tussen de € 700 en € 900,- bruto per maand.

Waarom IG&H?

Met meer dan 650 getalenteerde collega’s hebben we een unieke cultuur gecreëerd die zowel high caring als high daring is. We dagen elkaar uit om grenzen te verleggen, maar doen dat altijd vanuit vertrouwen, samenwerking en plezier.

Als deze stage bij je past, dan is IG&H een mooie plek om je verder te ontwikkelen. Je krijgt de kans om veel te leren in korte tijd, je eigen ideeën in te brengen en te ontdekken hoe het is om te werken binnen een consultancy- en technologieorganisatie waar AI volop in beweging is. Je werkt direct mee aan onderwerpen die relevant zijn voor de toekomst van IG&H en onze klanten.

Ben jij enthousiast geworden over deze stage binnen ons Data & AI-team?

Dan maken we graag kennis met je. Voor meer informatie kun je contact opnemen met ons recruitmentteam via

We willen dat onze medewerkers een afspiegeling zijn van de diversiteit in de samenleving. We werken samen met een opmerkelijke mix van talenten, persoonlijkheden en culturen. IG&H is trots een werkgever te zijn die gelijke kansen biedt. Alle gekwalificeerde sollicitanten worden in overweging genomen voor een stage of dienstverband, ongeacht nationaliteit, ras, religie, geslacht, genderidentiteit of -expressie, seksuele geaardheid, genetica, handicap of leeftijd. We geven om individualiteit, maar het belangrijkste is dat we trots zijn op onze collectieve prestaties en een Great Place to Work.

Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld. We werken met preferred suppliers. Stuur ons geen ongevraagde cv’s.

At Luscii, we work on several applications within the OMRON Digital Health Circle, including the Luscii Thuismeten app and OMRON Connect. Together with your future colleagues, we build technology that takes the burden off patients and healthcare professionals, creating more space for care. As an Android Developer, you will help make this happen by building and improving the mobile applications that connect people, devices and healthcare.

We create technology to make healthcare more accessible, as our digital health solutions help healthcare professionals monitor patients remotely, so people can receive the right care in the right place. As an Android Developer at Luscii, you will build and improve the mobile applications that make this possible.

Your work goes beyond writing code. You will help shape technical direction, share your expertise with colleagues and explore new technologies that can improve our apps. At Luscii, our Holacratic way of working also gives you the autonomy to take initiative, pick up responsibilities and contribute beyond your core role.

The applications you build need to work reliably in a healthcare context, where stability and usability matter. You are going to make sure that our apps remain performant, scalable and easy to maintain, while exploring new ways to improve the experience for patients and healthcare professionals. By combining solid engineering with thoughtful technical choices, you will help us continue to develop its digital healthcare platform.

Your role

As Android Developer at Luscii, you will combine hands-on development with technical ownership, working closely with colleagues across development, QA and support to build, improve and maintain our applications. You turn ideas into useful, intuitive digital health solutions. Whether you are exploring a new technology, building a proof of concept or solving a production issue, you will have the autonomy to make technical decisions and the opportunity to influence how we build our apps.

What you will be doing:

  • Develop and optimise Android applications in Kotlin, with a focus on performance, stability and user experience.

  • Shape mobile architecture and technical solutions, applying sound software design principles and patterns.

  • Build prototypes and proof of concepts to explore ideas and validate technical approaches early.

  • Develop features that communicate with Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) devices.

  • Investigate and resolve production issues, using debugging and performance analysis to keep our apps reliable.

  • Review code, share technical guidelines and collaborate with development, QA and support colleagues.

  • Explore relevant developments in mobile technology, including Jetpack Compose and Kotlin Multiplatform, and recommend improvements where they add value.

Why Luscii?

Read more about working at Luscii and how we work at Luscii/OMRON. Together, we are working on a mission to create space for care. Freedom, autonomy and ownership are of great importance in this. You are responsible for your own results and work according to the principles of Holacracy.

Most important benefits

  • Salary: € 4.600 - € 5.900 gross per month (based on 32 hours per week – that’s full-time at Luscii).

  • Remote-first: Work from anywhere in The Netherlands. We stay connected through monthly in-person team days called Assemblii.

  • Flexible setup: Create your own ideal workspace. Whatever works best for you - we’ve got you covered here.

The ideal candidate…

… probably doesn't exist, but if you can tick most of the checkboxes below, please apply! We are looking for somebody who is comfortable in taking ownership and making well-considered decisions independently. You enjoy the autonomy to shape your work and responsibilities, while actively seeking collaboration and alignment with others.

You know when to step up, when to involve colleagues and when to move forward decisively. Working independently does not mean working in isolation for you. You feel at ease being both a self-starter and a committed team player, contributing to shared goals while taking responsibility for your own domain. You value open communication, transparency, and mutual trust.

  • You have at least five years of experience in Android or mobile development and extensive experience with Kotlin, including coroutines and Flow.

  • You have a relevant bachelor’s degree in e.g. Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a comparable field, combined with experience working in an Agile environment.

  • You have experience with clean architecture, software design patterns and approaches such as MVVM or MVI, and you understand how to apply them in maintainable mobile applications.

  • You have experience with Jetpack Compose, mobile unit and/or UI testing, CI/CD pipelines and Android design guidelines.

  • You understand mobile performance and reliability, including memory management, multithreading, networking, debugging and optimisation, as well as working with web services, cloud platforms and APIs.

  • You are open to working in a Holacratic organization and curious about our way of organizing work, roles, and responsibilities;

  • English is our primary language for all internal communication at Luscii, so you're fluent in that language.

Interested? Apply now!

Would you like more information? Feel free to contact our recruiter Björn Bogerd via

What does the recruitment process look like?

We organise three interviews for each vacancy. It is an extensive process, but we want to ensure that there is a good fit in regards to a potential collaboration, our culture and our way of working. All interviews are conducted online and the entire procedure is planned in advance to keep momentum.

Freelance | Hybrid, Netherlands | Interim, immediate start 

Riverflex supports technology leaders at major organisations, and we're looking for an experienced Senior Consultant to join us on an interim basis. You'll work within a Riverflex team, alongside our in-house consultants and reporting into a Riverflex project lead. The client will know you as part of the Riverflex team, not as a standalone contractor. 

Current opportunity 

A leading European retailer is merging its regional technology departments. You'll work with the leadership team that reports to the CTO to shape, document and drive the convergence plan. That includes team changes, the case for funding and how the plan is communicated across the organisation.  

We're looking for a strong communicator with a top-tier consulting background. You'll pull ideas out of senior people's heads, structure them and turn them into a clear story. You also need to challenge the thinking so the message gets sharper. This is a strategy and storytelling role, not project management. 

About Riverflex 

Riverflex was founded in Amsterdam and London in 2018 and is now a global team of consultants helping courageous leaders drive intelligent transformation. We work across three pillars: strategy and transformation consulting, talent services, and AI products. www.riverflex.com

What you'll do 

  • You'll own a clear workstream within the wider Riverflex project, working daily with the project lead and the team and reporting on progress several times a week. 

  • You'll interview senior stakeholders and turn what you hear into a structured plan, a narrative and executive-ready materials. 

  • You'll run workshops that help client leaders agree on decisions, priorities and next steps. 

  • You'll challenge client thinking constructively, asking “what do you mean by that?” and “have you considered X?” so the final message holds up. 

  • You'll build storylines and slide decks for different audiences, from C-suite updates to communications for project teams. 

  • You'll re-plan quickly when priorities shift, and add value from week one. 

  • You'll uphold Riverflex's quality standards: your work is reviewed and joined into the wider team's deliverables before it reaches the client. 


Job requirements 

  • 5-7 years' experience, including strategy or technology consulting at an MBB or Big 4 firm, Accenture or similar 

  • Excellent PowerPoint and storytelling skills: you can turn complex, unstructured input into a sharp storyline 

  • Experience running workshops and stakeholder interviews 

  • Business change or change communications experience 

  • A collaborative, low-ego style, and comfortable working within a team and reporting into a project lead 

  • Available immediately; based in the Netherlands and able to be on site in Amsterdam around two days a week  

  • Fluent English and the right to work in the EU 

Nice to have

  • Experience with a post-merger integration or a reorganisation of technology teams 

  • Experience designing or running communications programmes 

  • Comfort using AI-enabled ways of working 

Why this role 

You'll do senior-level strategy work for a technology leadership team, with real input into the thinking from day one and the support of a Riverflex team around you. We have several engagements in progress, so strong delivery can lead to further interim work, and we're open to talking about permanent roles for the right people. 

Apply now 

Send us your CV and a short note on your most relevant experience, through Recruitee or by contacting our talent team. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to share three or more anonymised slide decks they created themselves before the interview. 

Riverflex is an equal opportunities employer and does not discriminate on any protected characteristic. If you don't meet every requirement but are excited about the role, we'd still love to hear from you.

About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.

About the role

We're hiring a Regional Vice President in EMEA to own and lead our Benelux and Nordics business. You'll inherit a team of four quota-carrying enterprise AEs across two hubs: Amsterdam and Stockholm and be responsible for building the management layer, operating model and partner ecosystem that takes both the Benelux and Nordics regions from early traction to consistent, scaled revenue.

This is a Director-level hire with second-line ambition. You'll report directly to the VP EMEA and operate with meaningful autonomy across pipeline, hiring, partner relationships and executive engagement.

 

What you'll own

Team leadership and performance

  • Lead, develop and expand the Enterprise Sales teams across Benelux and Nordics from day one

  • Run weekly pipeline reviews, deal coaching sessions and forecast calls with precision and consistency

  • Identify and close performance gaps early: coach the team to close larger deals faster and navigate complex, multi-stakeholder cycles

  • Build a culture of accountability and development; create clear career paths for senior individual contributors, including first-line management opportunities as the team scales

Revenue

  • Own the Benelux and Nordics regional number: quarterly and annual quota attainment across all two sub-regions

  • Build and maintain a healthy pipeline that supports consistent delivery and predictable forecasting to VP EMEA and leadership

  • Engage directly in strategic deals as executive sponsor, bringing credibility and commercial weight to enterprise negotiations

  • Establish the region's strongest lighthouse accounts across key industry verticals, building referenceable wins that anchor LangChain's market position in the Benelux and Nordics regions

Hiring

  • Manage multiple open roles across Benelux and Nordics simultaneously: owning the full hiring lifecycle across pipeline, assessment, and closing

  • Partner with the retained search firm and internal talent team to move at pace without compromising on quality

  • Define the headcount profile for Benelux and Nordics regions beyond Q1 and feed into H2 planning, ensuring the team is built ahead of the revenue curve

Partner ecosystem

  • Owns hyperscaler and GSI/RSI relationships (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, and key SIs) across UKI, Nordics and Benelux

  • Develop a structured partner motion that generates qualified pipeline and supports deal acceleration, reduces risk and drives expansion

  • Represent LangChain at partner QBRs and executive engagements in region

Market presence

  • Represent LangChain as a keynote-ready leader at partner events, customer engagements, and industry conferences across the region: including KubeCon, Money20/20, Nordic AI summits and customer EBCs

  • Build LangChain's brand with technical buyers, CIOs, and innovation leaders across Benelux and Nordics most important enterprise accounts

  • Bring intelligence on the Benelux and Nordics markets back to the VP EMEA and product teams to inform roadmap and go-to-market positioning

 

What we're looking for

Experience

  • 8+ years in enterprise SaaS sales, with at least 3 years in a regional or sub-regional leadership role managing quota-carrying AEs

  • Demonstrable track record of hitting and exceeding regional revenue targets across multiple quarters

  • Experience managing teams across multiple countries and time zones, with the cultural intelligence to operate across Benelux and Nordics

  • Background selling to technical buyers (engineering leaders, CTOs, platform teams): you understand how developer tools get evaluated and adopted

  • Experience in the AI, data, or developer tooling space strongly preferred; familiarity with the LangChain ecosystem is a meaningful plus

Leadership

  • You've run teams of 6+ AEs before and know the difference between managing and coaching

  • You can hold a forecast conversation with a VP and a deal coaching session with an AE in the same afternoon and add value in both

  • You hire well and fast. You know what good looks like for enterprise AE profiles and you can run structured hiring processes across four open roles simultaneously

  • You've built or contributed to a partner motion before: you understand what "partner pipeline" means in practice, not just in theory

Operating style

  • You bias toward action. You don't wait for a playbook to be handed to you: you build it

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity and early-stage scale. This is not a role with a fully defined motion; you'll shape a significant part of it

  • You communicate clearly and directly, to your team and to leadership

  • You're present in the market. You attend the right events, know the right people and build relationships that translate into pipeline and retention

     

Compensation Philosophy:

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Benefits

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Platform Engineer based in Netherlands.

Join a forward-thinking technology team building the AI platform that powers intelligent agents across multiple business functions, including engineering, business development, compliance, support, and finance. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you will design, develop, and operate the infrastructure that enables AI agents to perform increasingly autonomous tasks safely and reliably. You will work across agent runtimes, integrations, identity management, security guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and observability. Collaborating closely with internal domain experts, you will turn operational challenges into scalable AI-powered solutions that deliver measurable business value. You will take ownership from initial design and implementation through production deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement. This remote-first opportunity is ideal for an experienced engineer who combines strong software fundamentals with practical expertise in deploying and scaling LLM-based systems.


Accountabilities

You will help build and evolve the organization's AI platform, enabling teams across the business to deploy reliable, secure, and increasingly autonomous agents. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Productionizing AI workflows: Transform prototypes into robust production systems with defined service-level agreements (SLAs), supporting use cases such as specification-to-pull-request agents, AI-powered code reviews, incident triage, and Know Your Business (KYB) reviews.

  • Building and managing MCP servers: Design, deploy, secure, and maintain Model Context Protocol servers, including authentication, per-user OAuth, scoped access, and integrations with tools such as Slack, GitHub, Jira, HubSpot, and internal services.

  • Developing autonomous agents: Build multi-step agents capable of planning and taking action across different tools, progressing through controlled trust stages from shadowing and suggesting to executing tasks autonomously.

  • Implementing security and governance: Establish platform-wide guardrails, including agent identities, scoped credentials, audit logs, CI checks, approval workflows, allowlists, and least-privilege access policies.

  • Creating evaluation frameworks: Develop test datasets, evaluation criteria, regression suites, and live production scoring systems to measure agent quality and connect performance metrics to business outcomes.

  • Improving observability: Instrument agents and workflows with tracing, logging, latency and cost metrics, drift detection, alerts, and dashboards that help internal Operators monitor performance.

  • Managing AI expenditure: Track usage and spending across AI providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and OpenRouter. Establish budgets, alerts, and cost attribution at the team, agent, and workflow levels.

  • Supporting internal stakeholders: Work directly with Operators across business functions to understand their needs, develop requested features, create documentation, deliver enablement sessions, and build self-service tools.

  • Developing reusable AI capabilities: Create and maintain shared skills, plugins, and knowledge resources covering company processes, standards, security requirements, and brand guidelines.

  • Driving process automation: Proactively identify repetitive manual workflows that could benefit from AI, implement automation solutions, measure their impact, and continuously improve them.

  • Taking end-to-end ownership: Write technical specifications, plan and deliver projects independently, communicate progress asynchronously, and remain accountable for monitoring and improving solutions after deployment.

    • Requirements

    The ideal candidate combines strong software engineering fundamentals with hands-on experience building and operating production-ready AI systems. You should be comfortable working independently, communicating with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and applying sound judgment to complex automation and security challenges. Required qualifications include:

  • At least 5 years of experience as a software, platform, or infrastructure engineer, with a solid understanding of system design, data modeling, testing, debugging, and code review.

  • Between 6 and 12 months of experience shipping LLM-based systems to production and supporting agentic workflows used by real end users.

  • Daily, hands-on experience using AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex to write, test, and review production code.

  • Experience developing autonomous or multi-step agents with tool integrations, using technologies such as the Claude Agent SDK, Anthropic APIs, OpenAI APIs, or similar frameworks.

  • Practical experience building MCP servers, including OAuth authentication flows, scoped tokens, and user-level access controls.

  • Knowledge of identity and access management systems such as Okta or similar identity providers, including SSO protocols (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning, group-based access, and device policies.

  • Experience creating automated system identities, including GitHub Apps, service accounts, API keys, and managing secrets through tools such as 1Password.

  • Understanding of security guardrails and governance practices, including least-privilege access, audit logging, CI checks, approval gates, allowlists, and policy-as-code.

  • Experience designing evaluation systems for LLM applications, including test sets, evaluation rubrics, CI regression testing, release gates, and live production scoring.

  • Practical experience implementing production observability through tracing, metrics, alerting, and dashboards, using tools such as OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Datadog, Langfuse, LangSmith, or Braintrust.

  • Experience monitoring and controlling AI expenditure across providers through API key limits, cost centers, budgets, and actionable alerts.

  • Strong programming skills in at least one of TypeScript, Python, or Go, alongside working knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and cloud infrastructure.

  • A demonstrated ability to independently identify and automate manual processes, supported by two or three concrete examples of previous work.

  • Strong written communication skills, with the ability to produce clear technical specifications, runbooks, and RFCs.

  • Ability to understand stakeholder needs, translate ambiguous requests into actionable technical requirements, and explain complex concepts to both executives and subject matter experts.

  • A proactive and autonomous working style, with the ability to prioritize effectively, challenge unsafe or low-value requests constructively, and communicate progress across time zones.

  • A strong sense of ownership, including the ability to validate solutions with users, monitor performance after deployment, and continuously iterate.

    • Preferred Qualifications:

Functie  Reliability engineer

 

Beschrijving functie

 

De reliability engineer is een productie specialist die de totale levensduur van installatie bestudeert en analyseert hoe het bedrijf omgaat met investeringen en onderhoud van assets.  De reliability engineer is de expert in het identificeren van potentiële risico’s en het voorkomen van stilstanden. Daar problemen moeilijk volledig te voorkomen zijn, geeft de reliability engineer adviezen hoe te handelen bij storingen die plaatsvinden. Het doel is te voorkomen dat fouten in productiesystemen optreden.

 

De reliability engineer analyseert tevens de veiligheidsrisico’s geassocieerd met installatie fouten. Ter voorkoming van stilstand maakt de reliability engineer onderhoudsschema’s en analyseert statistische gegevens die helpen te voorspellen wanneer en hoe fouten voor kunnen komen. De reliability engineer ontwikkelt inspectie criteria die gebruikt worden om de asset health te monitoren. 



Om dit te kunnen bereiken maakt de reliability engineer gebruik van een aantal technieken.

 

  • Voorlopige gevaren analyse: Preliminary hazard analysis is de initiële identificatie van potentiële gevaren en fouten in een productie proces of systeem

  • Failure modes and effect analysis ( FMEA): Betreft het opsommen van de manieren dat een proces of systeem kan falen en wat de consequenties hiervan zijn.

  • Criticality analysis: bepaalt hoe ernstig de consequenties zijn van een asset fout voor het productiesysteem van het bedrijf.

  • Onderhoudbaarheid: gedetailleerde informatie hoe efficiënt en betrouwbaar het bedrijf een onderdeel kan repareren.

  • Foutenboom analyse: onderzoek van een systeem fout door naar de kleinere voorafgaande gebeurtenissen te kijken die hebben bijgedragen aan de systeem fout



    • Taken

    1. Trouble shooting

      1. Faciliteren van root cause analyse in geval van complexe, multidisciplinaire afwijkingen/storingen waar de uitvoerende teams niet uitkomen

      2. Daily problem solving

    2. Continue verbeteren

      1. Periodieke analyse op performance killers en cost drivers om van daaruit middels verbetervoorstellen bij te dragen aan een maximale beschikbaarheid & betrouwbaarheid van installaties tegen minimale kosten

      2. Innovatief denken m.b.t. het verlagen van de kosten en verhogen van de betrouwbaarheid

      3. Leiden/faciliteren van verbeterteams c.q. verbeterprojecten

    3. Change Management

      1. Beoordelen van wijzigingen op technische haalbaarheid met het bestaande machinepark. Vanuit procurement komen verzoeken op het gebied van grondstof wijzigingen ( andere leverancier, andere specificaties ed.) 

      2. Begeleiden van proeven vanuit de technische kant op de machines

      3. Installatie nieuwe machines / introductie nieuwe producten 

    4. Technische beschikbaarheid & betrouwbaarheid

      1. Evalueren van preventief onderhoud en voorstellen doen ter verbetering met als doel het verhogen van de beschikbaarheid van het machinepark

      2. Het verlagen van onderhoudskosten door het optimaliseren van onderhoudsconcepten en doorvoeren van technische verbeteringen.

    5. Investeringsprojecten

      1. Participeren in investeringsprojecten om de onderhoudbaarheid te borgen en het inregelen van onderhoud en spare parts.

      2. Inbrengen van technische kennis en ervaringen.

      3. Toezien op naleving van de standaard op gebied van onderdelen en installaties.

    6. Onderhoudsstrategie bepalen

      1. Opstellen van effectieve onderhoudsconcepten zodat onderhoud van de installaties op de meest efficiënte en effectieve manier kan worden gerealiseerd tegen zo laag mogelijke kosten

      2. Borgen van compliance; het inregelen van wettelijke inspecties en keuringen  en toezien op tijdige uitvoering daarvan.

    7. Beheren van de Standard Operating Procedures voor de installaties (SOP)

      1. Schrijven van nieuwe SOP’s, inclusief autonoom onderhoud

      2. Herzien van SOP’s als gevolg van proces verbeteringen en aanpassingen

    8. Bewaken standaarden voor veiligheid en kwaliteit

      1. Uitvoeren van risico assessments

      2. Borgen dat processen voldoen aan veiligheids standaarden en kwaliteits standaarden.

      3. Uitvoeren van optimalisatie testen.

      4. Ontwikkelen van best practice  die de productkwaliteit borgen
